<description>
{
 "summary": "Check block undo data availability before attempting to read undo data in the `/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` REST endpoint. If `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` is not set on the block index, the endpoint returns an HTTP 404 immediately without calling `ReadBlockUndo()`. A functional test verifies that querying a side-branch block returns a 404 without writing undo failure errors to `debug.log`.",
 "problem": "When `/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` is requested for a block that lacks undo data\u2014such as pruned blocks or disconnected side branches\u2014`ReadBlockUndo()` fails and logs an `[error] OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)` to `debug.log`. Although the REST endpoint correctly returns a 404 response, unauthenticated requests can spam the log with false error messages that mimic disk corruption.",
 "evidence": [
  "Commit and PR description: \"For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch) or whose undo data was pruned, GetUndoPos() is null, so OpenUndoFile() fails and ReadBlockUndo() writes 'OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)' to debug.log with LogError.\"",
  "PR description notes the test fails on master: \"The new check at the end of interface_rest.py requests a stale block and fails on master because of the logged error.\""
 ],

<category name="rpc" title="RPC / REST / ZMQ">
## Covers

The node's programmatic interfaces: JSON-RPC methods and their help and
argument handling, the HTTP server and authentication, `bitcoin-cli`,
the REST interface, and ZMQ notifications. Wallet RPCs are wallet first
and rpc second unless the change is to the RPC machinery itself. The
RPC/REST/ZMQ label is a strong prior.

Not rpc: the behavior an RPC merely exposes (that belongs to its area).

## What matters here

Compatibility first: changes that break or silently alter what existing
callers get back affect every application built on the node, so
correctness of returned data and the discipline around deprecations
matter most. Then security of the interface: authentication, exposure
of sensitive data, resource exhaustion through the HTTP server. Then
gaps that force applications into workarounds: missing fields or
methods that downstream software has asked for, with evidence they
asked. Then performance of hot methods that block explorers and
indexers call constantly. Then consistency and documentation of the
interface.

New methods without an external consumer asking rank low.
